item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Hey there! I go by "DrStinkyBacteriaV2" in tribute to my previous wikidot account "DrStinkyBacteria" which I have not accessed in over 2 years now. I've been into the SCP genre for over 3 years now and I have finally taken it upon myself to begin fantasizing on several ideas I have loathed over. But, I'm truly getting ahead of myself.

The real reason I finally decide to revive my previous wikidot account is because, well, I had written an entire SCP on the SCP Wiki Sandbox and never did anything with it; how foolish of me to allow such fantastic ideas go to waste, right? Anyways the ideas had some merit to them and I thought I'd revive them along with a set goal to have a long-standing within this genre.

But anyways, I currently have nothing better to do with my life, especially consider that it is Christmas Break for me at the moment, and Covid is giving me quite a bit of free time to say the least. I am quite frankly excited to get to encounter new people and I am also looking forward to endlessly typing on this site. Right now living in a tiny as hell duplex In-the-Middle-of-Nowhere, Tennessee and I'd say that I am having the time of my life, with my introverted self, at this computer.

Sorry for any grammar mistakes this may have, I have been up all night and I am writing this now at 3:35 AM.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Hello,

my pen name is Galvaude and I'm really looking into participating in this awesome community. I discovered the SCP Foundation through the "Infographic Show" short's. The video of SCP-1981 really made me want to dig more into the SCP universe and here I am!

I've always liked horror-ish stories with mind-breaking technology and moral twisting entities ; from Poe to Warhammer 40k. I am here to contribute to the SPC universe with, I hope, interesting content for the readers/community to enjoy. I have studied political science, more specificaly political philosohpy, and I believe this will show in my future SPC stories. I also really enjoy discussing ideas and concepts, so I'm willing to engage in any on-going discussions! English is not my first langage, although I had to learn it at a young age. My first langage is french (Canada).

As for my hobbies, I DM, I play videogames (mostly RPGs - Big fan of the Baldur's Gate saga), and write poetry, short stories, make experimental videos, etc… my hobbies are always artistic but with a situationnist touch (check out what is situationnism). This is one of the reason I joined this community ; I feel like the collective approach is definitly situationnist in it's nature (being collective and anonymous). I like it alot!

As for the SCP, I am definitly intrigued (more and more) about the Thaumiel class. I have read all the SCPs that are listed under this class and I am fascinated by the boundary between the Keter and Thaumiel class (like SCP-1968). I think I'm going to dig deeper into that relation and on how the foundation deals with that. If anyone would be kind enough to guide me through existing conflictual/boundary-crossing SPCs and potential debates on classes, that would be really nice :). Of course, this is not to proove that the S/E/K/T(N) system does not work, it is just that I like to swim in uncharted waters.

I am definitly looking into making SCP articles, and I really appreciate the peer-reviewed system that is established here.

As per the december question, I think my answer relates to the colours you see when you close your eyes. I always wonder if I can control them or not, and if I could control them, would the patterns be as pretty? And then I fall asleep lol

Cheers and Merry Christmas lol
-Galvaude

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Hey all. My name's John, and I'm a teenager living in Michigan, USA.

I've known about the Foundation for years now, and it's been long enough that I don't remember exactly how I discovered it, although it was probably through watching Let's Plays of Containment Breach back in the day. This community seems like a welcoming place, but I'm not quite sure what I want to do here, whether it be writing SCPs or just reading and giving my input.

In real life, I like learning about history and government, and just researching things in general. More recently, I've started to get into graphic design and perhaps even architecture, which seems like a good career to go into.

What keeps me up at night is mostly my imagination. I usually either place myself in fictional scenarios, or use fictional characters to carry out said scenarios. These scenarios I create usually revolve around something that interests me or whatever occupied my time that day. Hopefully I can utilize my creativity and put it to good use here.

I'm glad to be finally joining the site after all these years, and I'm looking forward to contributing to the community.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Hello everyone! I'm Ross - although you can call me Mira too, if you'd like!

I'm 20 years old, and I've been been a casual reader of SCP articles for what must be almost five or six years now. Recently, though, I've delved far deeper into the assorted canons and some of the less "popular" articles, and I'm amazed by just how much the site really has to offer.

I enjoy the tone of the SCP Wiki on the whole - the general style is one that I am not particularly good at writing, but enjoy reading to a great extent. The creativity on display in exploring concepts from the harmlessly light-hearted to the ones so horrifying that they have stuck with me for years is nothing short of admirable. (Perhaps one day, I'll workshop an idea of my own, but that isn't likely to happen for a very long time.)

As far as hobbies go, I enjoy character design and writing, and as some have likely deduced from my username, I'm a huge fan of visual novels as well. I also like baking, although most baked goods tend to be a little too sweet for my personal tastes.

With regards to what kind of random thoughts keep me up at night, they tend to range from something as mundane as having a song stuck in my head to whatever catastrophic situations my tired, anxious mind is able to come up with. Typically, though, they'll just jump from one topic of interest to another - usually if I've read something I really enjoyed, I won't be able to stop thinking about it.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers

Hi there, I'm Luggy.
I haven't posted on here in years so I thought I may as well re-introduce myself.

I discovered SCP a long time ago through the numerous fan-games that it spawned. Back then, I joined the site to improve my English and try to write for the site. However, I was also a teen who had no idea of what he was doing, so that didn't go very far. It's only recently that I rediscovered the site thanks to channels like TheVolgun and The Exploring Series and it has renewed my love for the site.

Writing an SCP when you're 17 sounds great, but now that I'm older, my goals have changed. I just want to hang out here and maybe improve my writing while I'm at it. If you guys got any suggestions regarding the latter, I'd love to hear them.

As far as hobbies go, my main hobby is drawing. I'm not great at it, but it's still something I'm passionate about. You can check out my art on Newgrounds.
Despite being an English major (in France), I still need to read more. Forcing people to read books you don't care about does that to you.

What kind of random thoughts keep me up at night ? Most likely all my old posts on here that have been buried by time. Crazy how a person can change in a few years.

Hoping I'll hang out longer here. Cheers !

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
I'm a 39 year old Community Minister with a philosophy degree and a heavy interest in table top roleplaying games.

A couple of years ago I was volunteering to run roleplaying games at a local high school, and in creating a game setting a couple of the kids mentioning drawing on the SCP setting for influence. When I asked what that was they described it as a collaborative writing project, which I assumed was something they were working on for class. I didn't ask any follow up questions. Six months later I stumbled upon some SCP youtube videos (with some not-really SCP videos, like Sirenhead and creepypastas) and ended up watching quite a few of them, mostly The Volgun and Eastside Show. That's become part of my routine now, when folding laundry or on the treadmill.

I mentioned rpgs as a hobby, but they're also a significant part of my work. I use them extensively in my ministry, as a community building tool and as an educational tool. It was probably inevitable then that I'd end up running a game set in the (well 'an') SCP Universe, and started doing so last Monday. I'm in the process of creating a website for our 'SCP: Outpost 108' campaign. I have a question along those lines; I want to put up some useful intro links, and I was wondering what other people thought should go on that list of links. So far I have a link to each of the following: The SCP Wiki, The SCP Wikipedia page, the wiki glossary page, the wiki security levels page, and the wiki MTF page.

We're not using any of the specific established canons, so this is 'mainline' SCP stuff.

Hi! I'm Kleo.
I go by he/him or they/them pronouns, both are equally fine.

Why/how did I join the site
I've been lurking on-and-off here for years. Not sure how long exactly, but long enough that I can't remember how I first found the SCP community. It's occupied a part of my mind for a long time. I've had some ideas for anomalies, and also wanted to vote on some criminally good posts, so I've decided to make an account.

Probably lurking for the most part. Commenting occasionally. Possibly writing. I'm not sure what combination of those things I'll do, so I'm using this thread instead of writing or reading. I've also got a list of skips that I've been intending to upvote.

+ show block
– hide block

I enjoy reading and watching films, particularly horror, thrillers, and sci-fi (no surprise there). What kind of random thoughts keep you up at night?
Typically, just imagining hypothetical scenarios and deciding how they'd play out. Not sure why I do this, but I have been doing it for as long as I can remember. Also, as of late, something resembling depression. This is what zero physical interaction does to a mf.
(Seriously though quarantine has been absolutely horrible for my mental health, as I'm sure it has been for everyone else. I'm not used to being constantly unhappy, or even anything less than optimistic. Ever since [REDACTED]virus made it so I can't talk to people in person, I realized how much I rely on those interactions for my happiness.)

That's about it. Probably a slog to read because I'm not a great writer. Hopefully it wasn't too bad.

Hi there!

My name is Atlas (they/them), though I'll respond to pretty much anything. I got into SCP pretty recently thanks to a friend who writes stuff around here. I've been browsing the wiki pretty much constantly for the past two or so weeks. I'm not really sure I'll do much here besides lurk, but that might change at some point in the future. Who knows?

I spend most of my time playing video games and acting as a father to my two rat sons and my dog daughter. My other interests include MGS, fighting games, and music history. I also still have a plethora of German trivia carved into my brain from the four years I spent in German classes during high school.

Every night, I'm kept awake by a plague of self-doubt and fear that I will never amount to anything or achieve any goal I may set for myself in life. What if every dream and aspiration I've ever had has been perfectly achievable and the only thing keeping me from succeeding is myself? What if I do achieve the goal I think I want, only to realize that I only pursued it because it was easy, and my real goal is so much higher? What if I die before I figure out what I truly want in life?

Anyway, I'm very excited to finally be here and maybe put my overactive anxiety brain to use!

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
How is everyone doing?

My name is Joel.

Anyways, why am I here? Well, you can probably thank the Youtube video blogger Ekhert's Ladder for that. I was watching one of his videos, and found myself here, obsessively reading entries. Some have been better than others, but there have been others that have been inspiring, creative, and even downright iconic (SCP-682, what I call The Plot Armor Reptile, SCP-1342, or what I call: What NOT to do to your Closest, Possibly Only Ally, SCP-1000 Bigfoot, SCP-2273, or what I call YOU MANIACS and YOU BLEW IT UP!!!, etc.).

As someone who loves themes that explores extraterrestrial life, alternate universe, running gags (again, SCP-682), and more emotional themes, such as hope and fear, and cruelty and morality (Foundation seems to be somewhat lacking in far the latter, and has ample amounts of in the one before that), the SCP multiverse is a fascinating medium for exploring such concepts. And yes, I'm a huge nerd, who will without hesitation make TV culture references.

I hope to write one or two entries, since it isn't like I don't have at least one idea for an SCP. As for whether or not I actually complete it is another matter, since I have hobbies in drawing/Photoshop/Illustrator, and more than occasionally in video games, and hope to go back to school, and begin a major Political Science next season. Not to mention I'd need to stop reading entries long enough to write something of substance!

Don't expect me to write any stories of gore and dark creatures in darkened hallways here to steal the souls of any Mobile Task Forces foolish enough to try to capture him, and disembowel any researcher foolish enough to refer to him by "it" or "SCP" though. Do expect content like an alternate instance of SCP-682 getting a cameo, and being dragged out, kicking, screaming, and shouting threats to something that doesn't consider it welcome. Because that is my sense of humor.

The only thing that seems to keep me up at night is on nights where I know that I have to get up early in the morning, but my brain won't SHUT DOWN ALREADY! Oddly enough, knowing that my part time job isn't enough to afford to move out, and that it will take at least two years to do something about it does not keep me up, even though it probably should.

Hello there, tordzak. Welcome to the SCP Wiki!

If you're interested in horror, history, and all that, I recommend you check out our IRC chatrooms. There, you can talk with people from the community about a wide variety of topics. Not only that, but you can make some great friends on there. If you do decide to join and you have troubles connecting, feel free to ask for help in the #site17 channel. Anyways, here's some stuff you may want to check out when getting started:

Navigation:

+ show block
– hide block

If you want to keep up with the latest material, check out the Most Recently Created page. If you'd rather check out only the most popular new articles, then Top Rated New Pages is the way to go.

While you're browsing, if you find an article you absolutely love, you can try finding more from the same author by looking them up on the Authors' Page hub. If the user in question is not on that list, you can try searching for them on our statistic site, scpper.com.

If there are some SCPs that you're a fan of, you can try checking out a new addition to the wiki: the SCP Series Tales List, created by yours truly. These are pages that mirror the main SCP listings, but they include all the stories that feature each SCP (for example, one can find everything that has been written about SCP-173).

Recommendations:

+ show block
– hide block

With the amount of SCPs we have, it can be hard to find really good articles in specific genres (not to mention we have no way of searching by genre), so I took it upon myself to curate a few lists of some good representative material to share with other users. With the help of various community members, User-Curated Lists has been built to facilitate fun wikiwalks of some amazing content!

With that said, I hope you enjoy your time here.

Note: If you're going to introduce yourself here, please scroll down and click "New Post" and NOT "reply", otherwise your comment will nest incorrectly!

Hello, new site members/artists/gamers/social media watchers/roleplayers/etc.!

This month's random question is: what kind of random thoughts keep you up at night?

Here's some places to talk to get you all started off, now that you've arrived:

  • Games and Hobbies forum: Just started playing a new game or are wondering if any other SCP site members play your favorite game? Alternatively, wondering if anyone else paints minifigures or goes to conventions? Jump into the conversations here.
  • Media Discussion forum: Have a cool video or news article that just screams of the paranormal? Talk about it and other such things here!
  • Fan Work forum: Have a cool drawing or want to see the work of some of the other artists here? Have an SCP-based mod or board game in the works? This is the place to discuss!

If you're not sure what to talk about here, you can take a look at our How to Write an Intro/Welcome thread for ideas.

Have fun mingling with the other new arrivals and talking about your interests, hobbies, and plans for taking over the universe. You might also see some of our veteran users here from time to time, since you never know when someone might be looking for an artist or a voice actor or an idea-haver for the next big collaboration article or SCP project! Talk and be merry. :)

Welcome to the site!
